issue_context.title: systemctl edit results in final missing final newline
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

247.3-7+deb11u1, 251.6-1

### Used distribution

Debian bullseye, sid

### Linux kernel version used

5.10.0-19-amd64, 6.0.0-2-amd64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

amd64, x32

### Component

systemctl

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

/e/s/s/*svc*.s.d/o.c to be a text file.

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

It isn't.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

`systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online`, put in some stuff, `cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf`, behold

I guess they don't *need* to be text files for systemd to accept them, but it's damn annoying, and means you can't process them in the usual ways.

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

I can confirm from some older overrides that they *used* to be text files, so idk.
comments:
Could you give some example? I just tried on a couple of machines, but don't see any issue:

Arch Linux, systemd 251.7-4 (`EDITOR=vim`)
```
# systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online
...
# cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
[Unit]
Description=hello
# file /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
/etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf: ASCII text
```

Fedora Rawhide, systemd-252~rc3-586.fc38.x86_64 (`EDITOR=nano`)
```
# systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online
...
# cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
foo bar
# file /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
/etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf: ASCII text, with no line terminators
```

Fedora 37, systemd-251.6-609.fc37.x86_64 (`EDITOR=vim`)
```
# systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online
...
# cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
hello
world
# cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
/etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf: ASCII text
```

or

```
# EDITOR=vim systemctl edit systemd-networkd-wait-online
...
# cat /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
[Unit]
Description=ěšěádfs§)š3
# file /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf 
/etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf: Unicode text, UTF-8 text
```

On both systems above I get:
```
nabijaczleweli@tarta:~$ cat -A /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd-wait-online.service.d/override.conf
ExecStart=$
ExecStart=/lib/systemd/systemd-networkd-wait-online --timeout=300nabijaczleweli@tarta:~$
```
after typing in both lines (default editor that resolves to vim.nox and nvi, respectively). Attaching typescript from sid system above: [typescript.gz](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/files/9964816/typescript.gz) (note also how GNU ed starts with "Newline appended" here, but of course that doesn't really matter for the temporary file, so whatever).

review_comments:
Won't this cause issues with editors that don't know the `+X` syntax? From top of my head I can think of `ed` or `cat`, which is not a very "real world" scenario, but maybe other editors will choke up as well?

```
$ EDITOR=cat sudo -E build/systemctl edit --runtime sshd.service
cat: +4: No such file or directory
### Editing /run/systemd/system/sshd.service.d/override.conf
### Anything between here and the comment below will become the new contents of the file



### Lines below this comment will be discarded

### /usr/lib/systemd/system/sshd.service
# [Unit]
# Description=OpenSSH server daemon
# Documentation=man:sshd(8) man:sshd_config(5)
# After=network.target sshd-keygen.target
# Wants=sshd-keygen.target
# 
# [Service]
# Type=notify
# EnvironmentFile=-/etc/sysconfig/sshd
# ExecStart=/usr/sbin/sshd -D $OPTIONS
# ExecReload=/bin/kill -HUP $MAINPID
# KillMode=process
# Restart=on-failure
# RestartSec=42s
# 
# [Install]
# WantedBy=multi-user.target(editor) failed with exit status 1.
```

or 

```
# Old systemctl
$ echo -ne '2a\nhello\n.\nw\n' | EDITOR=ed sudo -E systemctl edit --runtime sshd.service
Newline appended
648
654
$ cat /run/systemd/system/sshd.service.d/override.conf 
hello

# New systemctl
$ echo -ne '1a\nhello\n.\nw\n' | EDITOR=ed sudo -E build/systemctl edit --runtime sshd.service
122
128
$ cat /run/systemd/system/sshd.service.d/override.conf 
cat: /run/systemd/system/sshd.service.d/override.conf: No such file or directory
```
expecting every user's configured editor to be vi-like is a certified "lol" moment, for sure

emacs, nano, vi, pico, joe, … all support the "+" command line syntax for jumping to files too.

"cat" is not an editor. And "ed" is maybe a thought experiment at best.

Not sure we should hold back things just because of niche tools that people just use for the sake of using niche tools...

or to say this differently, maybe if people really want to use "ed" as an edito, they write a script thta eats up the "+" stuff and execs the real thing, and then set $EDITOR to that...

So here's the thing: if you hit "v" in "less", then it invokes $VISUAL/$EDITOR with the "+" syntax. If "less" can do that, then so can we.

I guess "less" is quite a standardizing force...
"maybe if people want systemd to use the editor they have configured they should change that editor". yeah, maybe. probably not tho.
so here's another thing: less doesn't care the least bit about how the editor returns (and you're unlikely to ever even see an error output!), `systemctl edit` errors out if the editor errors out.
If all the common editors support the syntax, let's use it.
